street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha), margins in percent; VA labels: FY2026 = company fiscal 2025 ending Feb 2026 (reported), FY2027 = company fiscal 2026 (the algorithm year). No margin level was ever stated, so gap_bps is null. Consensus fiscal 2026 EBITDA $3.588B sits 9.8% below the algorithm floor of fiscal 2025 EBITDA $3.9015B grown 2% (data_compute).

evidence_of_progress.note: Adjusted EBITDA margin from VA quarterly actuals: 4QFY-2026 (Q4 fiscal 2025, includes 53rd week) -8.8 bps yoy; 1QFY-2027 (Q1 fiscal 2026) -40.3 bps yoy, adj EBITDA $1.013B vs $1.111B. Fiscal 2026 EBITDA guide cut on 2026-07-23 to $3.55B to $3.625B, below fiscal 2025 actual $3.9015B, versus the algorithm of EBITDA growth above 2%+ ID sales. Wrong direction so far.

verdict: Mechanical 8/10 overstates the fit: leadership is turning over hard (internal CEO 2025-05, external Executive Chair Meg Whitman 2026-09, CFO search, 4 new directors) and the stock is cheap, but management never framed a margin level, its only numeric frame (2%+ IDs and faster EBITDA growth in fiscal 2026) was abandoned with a July 2026 guide cut, and the -8.8% EBITDA revision sits just inside the -10% line, so this reads as a story being reset rather than an unproven margin plan.
open_questions: Does Whitman as Executive Chair plus the permanent CFO hire bring a new numeric margin or EBITDA framework (Investor Day), or a strategic alternatives process (Wells Fargo asked about it on the 2026-07-23 call)?
How much of the $2B three-year productivity program and the $200M ACI Edge runway drops to EBITDA versus being reinvested in price, given fiscal 2026 EBITDA is guided down?
Has the EBITDA revision crossed -10% after Q2 fiscal 2026 results in October, which would flip D to 0 (story broken, not unproven)?
